findings.text: The routed object is a slice of a named test vector table where each element joins a title with an instruction sequence held in a union for classic or internal encodings, a mode word distinguishing classic from internal plus option flags, a sample input byte collection, an expected outcome collection of index and value pairs, and for negative checks a helper slot plus an expected error number.

Positive internal vectors in this slice use internal mode with empty input and one expectation anchored at index zero. They initialize the ten general registers, apply arithmetic, logical, shift or move operations in immediate and register forms, and guard progress with equality branches that fall through toward later checks on success and exit early on mismatch.

The visible tail of the 32-bit addition vector requires staged accumulated totals to match successive gates at 4063, 12177, 36518, 109540, 328605 and 985799, then moves the final accumulation into the result register for an overall expectation of 2957380.

Subtraction starts from zero through nine, gates an early value of minus fifty five, performs per register chained subtractions with an immediate ten, then negates and subtracts again for a final eleven. Multiplication starts from eleven then one through nine, gates 439084800, checks shifted high and low halves, and ends with a large final word. Exclusive or repeatedly proves self subtraction and self exclusive or both yield zero for a final one.

Register move and long immediate load vectors each propagate an all ones 64 bit pattern down the register chain, then clear every register with width specific zero moves or zero long loads, accumulate the cleared registers and add a fixed constant for a shared final value of 0xfefe. Mixed arithmetic gates divide and modulo results before returning minus one, and register counted shifts cover logical right, logical left and arithmetic right with several mid gates before returning minus one.

On 32 bit builds only, an extra internal vector checks context pointer handling by requiring a zero incoming word to stay zero and a nonzero incoming word to expose zero in the upper half after move and shift operations, with a final expectation of one.

Classic checker vectors define a validation rejection path: a program with no return, a divide by immediate zero, an instruction disallowed in socket filter context, a spill outside the scratch range, or a return of the index register alone or after loading it, is refused during checking with an invalid argument failure and no execution.

One positive classic vector runs a long sequence of half word absolute loads and conditional jumps with sparse targets over an Ethernet plus IP plus UDP shaped packet and expects acceptance with length 88 and value 0x001b. The scratch memory vector walks slots zero through fifteen, each step storing the index register, reloading it, converting to accumulator, incrementing, converting back and storing onward.

Several internal and scratch vectors are annotated as mainly exercising just in time compilation, so equivalent interpreter and compiled behavior is required and a code generation divergence on the pinned gates or final values counts as failure.
